details.title: Swan Lake (Paris Opera Ballet 2026 - 2027)
details.description:
Broadway Cinemas is proud to exclusively present the Paris Opera Ballet's spectacular 2026-2027 season! Kicking this season off are two world-renowned ballet classics coming straight to the big screen: Romeo and Juliet and Swan Lake.

 

Prince Siegfried is urged by his parents to choose a bride, but by the shores of a lake he meets a mysterious swan maiden, Odette, enchanted by the sorcerer Rothbart. Only a sincere vow can save her. Captivated, he swears eternal love, until he meets Odile, the black swan...

 

A magical ballet set to Tchaikovsky's sparkling music, Swan Lake was first created in 1877 for the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow, later restaged by Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov. Nearly a century later, Rudolf Nureyev brought his own interpretation to the Paris Opera in 1984.

details.description: Before the world had the vocabulary, San Francisco had the âgendernautsâ. At the giddy height of the late-90s tech boom, Monika Treut embedded herself among the Bay Area's community of trans and gender-fluid artists, activists and academics: historian Susan Stryker, "Goddess of Cyberspace" Sandy Stone, video artists Texas Tomboy and Jordy Jones, intersex activist Hida Viloria, and the irrepressible Annie Sprinkle. details.description: Grief has a way of following you across oceans. Hamburg artist Sophie Schmitt is undone by the sudden, unexplained death of her young Taiwanese lover, Ai-ling, and travels to Taipei with a video installation built in her memory. There she is pursued by Mei-li, a beguiling and persistent journalist who wants far more than an interview, and who soon materialises, unannounced, on Sophie's Hamburg doorstep. As seduction shades into investigation, past and present blur, and Monika Treut's cross-cultural mystery drifts elegantly toward the supernatural, steeped in Taiwanese ghost lore and the ache of unfinished love. The first German-Taiwanese co-production, shot between the night markets of Taipei and the grey light of Hamburg, GHOSTED premiered in the Berlinale's Panorama and remains one of Treut's most atmospheric works: a sapphic ghost story where the dead, like desire, refuse to stay buried.

details.description: Few films can claim to have started a revolution. details.name: Two Mothers (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Two Mothers (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: At the age of 57, Rosa von Praunheim's 94-year-old mother told him a secret that rewrote his life: he was adopted. Only after the death of Gertrud, the woman who raised the enfant terrible of German cinema with unconditional love, did he dare to look for his biological mother, armed with little more than the name of a Riga children's home. What unfolds is a detective story through the darkest chapter of European history, leading through the archives of Nazi-occupied Latvia and the spectre of SS eugenics to a birth certificate discovered in a prison hospital, and to a biological mother whose fate proves devastating. Germany's great provocateur turns the camera unflinchingly on himself and finds his most tender register: part whodunit, part reckoning with the Second World War, and above all a love letter to the mother who chose him. TWO MOTHERS was a jury award nominee at Tribeca.

details.description: Dorothee MÃ¼ller has a problem: she's a Hamburg journalist researching romantic love, and she can't find a shred of it. Ditching her dysfunctional relationships (and a hormone specialist's baffling theories), she flies to San Francisco in search of her runaway mother, and tumbles instead down the rabbit hole of the city's lesbian demi-monde, guided by strip-show barker Susie Sexpert (real-life sex guru Susie Bright) and magnetic drag king Ramona (Shelly Mars). Shot in luminous black-and-white by the great Elfi Mikesch, Monika Treut's sex-positive picaresque scandalised feminists and censors alike in 1988 and has since ripened into an underground classic: part German-expressionist satire, part sapphic travelogue, all liberation. Ina Blum is irresistible as the wide-eyed pilgrim who came looking for love and found her libido. The dildo lecture alone is worth a ticket.

details.name: The Einstein of Sex (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: The Einstein of Sex (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: Long before Kinsey, there was Magnus Hirschfeld: physician, sexologist, socialist, Jew, homosexual, and the man the tabloids dubbed "the Einstein of Sex." Rosa von Praunheim's affectionate biopic charts Hirschfeld's extraordinary crusade as he founds the world's first gay rights organisation in 1897, battles Paragraph 175, and opens Berlin's pioneering Institute for Sexual Science in 1920, a haven for queer and trans lives that flourished through the Weimar years until Nazi students torched its library in 1933. Friedel von Wangenheim plays the doctor with owlish warmth, flanked by his aristocratic great love Baron von Teschenberg, devoted young Karl Giese, and the institute's guardian angel, housekeeper Dorchen. Mixing period drama, newsreel and von Praunheim's trademark impish humour, it is both a monument to a man the Nazis nearly erased from history and a reminder of how quickly hard-won progress can burn.

A festival favourite, winning prizes at Goldener Spatz, Zlin and Giffoni.

details.description: Young German-Korean prosecutor Seyo Kim is determined to bring far-right extremists to justice in Germany. With a commanding debut performance by Chen Emilie Yan in the lead role, the film premiered in the Panorama section of the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival, taking home three prizes.

Across two years of recurring rides, Hassan begins to recognise echoes of his own buried pain, and is finally pushed to confront the past that led him to leave his homeland thirty years ago. details.title: Plan 75
details.description: In a near-future Japan, government programme Plan 75 encourages senior citizens to be voluntarily euthanized to remedy a super-aged society. After being laid off due to her age, an elderly woman considers joining the program. Surrounding her is a governmental structure built to enact the program. Inside, a young civil servant gently recruits candidate, a hotline counsellor listens patiently to the final words of the elderly, and a Filipino laborer tidies the left-behind belongings of the deceased. Within this closed loop of life, everyone is trying their best to survive, yet the threat of death looms closer, awaiting chance to devour the life of elderly. The debut feature of Chie Hayakawa points to the imminent social issue of ageing population, contemplating the weight of life. Cannes Camera d'Or Special Mention.

details.name: Father Mother Sister Brother
details.title: Father Mother Sister Brother
details.description:
Family reunion dinner hits different when you grow up â Cringe as you rehearse the conversation in your head a thousand times before turning the knob, and putting on a show.

 

Indie legend Jim Jarmusch brings together a star-studded cast featuring Adam Driver, Cate Blanchett, Charlotte Rampling, among others, to deliver a deadpan and heartwarming family drama that clinched the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival. The three stories all concern the relationships between adult children, their somewhat distant parent (or parents), and each other. Each of the three chapters takes place in the present, and each in a different country. FATHER is set in the Northeast US, MOTHER in Dublin, Ireland, and SISTER BROTHER in Paris, France. Echoing the episodic structure of his early classics, the film captures the delicate dance of modern relationships, at times intimate and at times distant, shaped by tentative steps and the unexpected warmth that hits you hard and soft.

details.description:
Douzi, a boy with feminine features, is abandoned by his prostitute mother to an all-boys Peking opera troupe supervised by Master Guan. Douzi befriends fellow trouper Shitou.

A few years later in 1938, a teenage Douzi is trained to play dan (female roles), while Shitou learns jing (painted face male roles). When practicing the play "Dreaming of the World Outside the Nunnery", Douzi intentionally mistakes the line "I am by nature a girl, not a boy" with "I am by nature a boy, not a girl," subjecting himself to severe physical punishments. Douzi along with another student, Laizi, attempt to run away, but Douzi decides to pursue acting seriously after witnessing an opera performance. Upon returning, they find the whole troupe being punished for their desertion, and Douzi is beaten. As a result, Laizi hangs himself...
